title: Opposite injective-simplex inclusion preserves cocone spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams and right-pinched Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes enlarged as necessary. For a small simplicial set $X$, let $\mathsf S(X)$ be the ordinary category whose objects are all simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, including degenerate simplices, and whose morphisms $\sigma\to\tau$ are monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\tau\Delta(\alpha)=\sigma$; composition is composition of the monotone maps. Let $\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)\subseteq\mathsf S(X)$ have all the same objects and only those morphisms for which $\alpha$ is injective; its objects still include degenerate simplices of $X$. Let
$$j_X:N(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}})\longrightarrow N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}})$$
be induced by inclusion. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, every map $p:N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}})\to\mathcal E$ and every vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_{N(\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}})}T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal E)}(pj_X,\Delta_{N(\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}})}T).$$
No quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ or colimit-existence hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is imposed; the empty case is included.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, step (3), printed pp. 255-256, using Lemma 6.5.3.7 and Proposition 4.1.2.15; Proposition 4.1.1.7, printed p. 226, and natural join/cocone comparison for the mapping-space formulation. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}$, $D=\mathsf S(X)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and let $u:A\to D$ be inclusion, so $j_X=N(u)$. These are small ordinary categories: their objects form $\coprod_{n\geq0}X_n$, and their arrows are subsets of the products of these sets with sets of finite monotone maps. Their nerves are quasicategories: an inner horn in an ordinary nerve fills by composition of its arrows, and the category laws give the required higher faces. If $X=\varnothing$, both categories are empty and $j_X$ is the identity of the empty simplicial set. Restriction is then the identity on the two identical mapping spaces, which are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Henceforth it suffices to verify the comma hypothesis for each object $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$ of $D$.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, step (3); definitions and the empty case. Online primary source inspected 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Fix $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$. Define an ordinary category $C_n$ whose objects are ALL monotone maps $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ with $m\geq0$. A morphism $\theta\to\theta'$ is an injective monotone $a:[m]\hookrightarrow[m']$ satisfying $\theta' a=\theta$. The ordinary comma category $(\sigma\downarrow u)$ is exactly $C_n^{\mathrm{op}}$. Indeed an object of the comma is an arrow $\sigma\to\tau$ in $D$, hence an operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ with $\tau=\sigma\Delta(\theta)$. Conversely this formula defines its object for EVERY $\theta$, even if different operators have the same simplex in $X$, since the operator is part of the comma object. A comma morphism from $\theta$ to $\theta'$ is an arrow $\tau\to\tau'$ in $A$, hence an injective $a:[m']\hookrightarrow[m]$ with $\theta a=\theta'$. This is precisely the reverse of the corresponding arrow in $C_n$; identities and composition are the same operator compositions. This identification uses neither injectivity of $\sigma$ nor nondegeneracy of any simplex.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.5.3.7, proof: the category of operators into [n]; applied directly over a fixed simplex of X. Online primary source inspected 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Here is the contraction, including all operators. Let $b:[0]\to[n]$ take $0$ to $0$, and let $B:C_n\to C_n$ be constant at $b$. Define $H:C_n\to C_n$ by prepending $0$: for $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, set $H(\theta):[m+1]\to[n]$ by $H(\theta)(0)=0$ and $H(\theta)(i+1)=\theta(i)$. For $a:\theta\to\theta'$, set $H(a)(0)=0$ and $H(a)(i+1)=a(i)+1$. This is injective and monotone, and $H(\theta')H(a)=H(\theta)$ at $0$ and at every $i+1$; its formulas preserve identities and composites. There are natural transformations $B\Rightarrow H\Leftarrow\mathrm{id}_{C_n}$: the component of the first is $0\mapsto0$, and that of the second is $i\mapsto i+1$. Naturality follows respectively from $H(a)(0)=0$ and $H(a)(i+1)=a(i)+1$. All component operators are injective. In particular this still works at $n=0$ and for constant or otherwise degenerate $\theta$; $H(\theta)$ need not be nondegenerate, which is why all simplices were retained.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.5.3.7, proof, printed p. 676: the prepended-vertex functor and its two natural transformations, with formulas expanded. Online primary source inspected 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Taking opposites gives the zigzag $B^{\mathrm{op}}\Leftarrow H^{\mathrm{op}}\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_{C_n^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Apply [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] directly to this opposite category, without assuming a comparison of realizations with opposite nerves: the two transformations give homotopies joining its identity to the constant map at $b$. Equivalently the unique functor $P:C_n^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf1$ and the functor $Q:\mathbf1\to C_n^{\mathrm{op}}$ selecting $b$ have $PQ=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf1}$ and the displayed zigzag from $QP=B^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the identity. The cited theorem says $NP$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus $N(\sigma\downarrow u)=N(C_n^{\mathrm{op}})$ is weakly contractible. The chosen $b$ ensures nonemptiness.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.5.3.7, last paragraph of proof, with the contraction applied directly to the opposite comma category. Online primary source inspected 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: We verify that this ordinary comma computes the infinity-categorical comma required below. For an ordinary category $D$, the coherent undercategory $N(D)_{\sigma/}$ is $N(D_{\sigma/})$: a simplex consists of a chain beginning with an arrow from $\sigma$, and the undercategory identities are exactly its commuting triangles. The projection $N(D_{\sigma/})\to N(D)$ is an isofibration. For an inner-horn lifting problem, the given chain in $D_{\sigma/}$ has its unique nerve filler, obtained by composing adjacent arrows. Its projection agrees with the prescribed base simplex because both fill the same inner horn in $N(D)$ and such a filler is unique in an ordinary nerve; an equivalence in $N(D)$ is an ordinary isomorphism, and an isomorphism $e:d\to d'$ lifts at $h:\sigma\to d$ by the arrow from $h$ to $eh$ over $e$, with its inverse over $e^{-1}$. Both nerves are small quasicategories. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] to this projection and $N(u):N(A)\to N(D)$. Its conclusion identifies the strict pullback $N(A)\times_{N(D)}N(D_{\sigma/})$ with the infinity-categorical pullback. Degree by degree the strict pullback is $N(\sigma\downarrow u)$: its simplices are chains of objects of $A$ with arrows from $\sigma$ commuting with those chains. Step 4 therefore gives weak contractibility of the infinity-categorical comma $N(A)\times^h_{N(D)}N(D)_{\sigma/}$ for every $\sigma$.

source.place: HTT Theorem 4.1.3.1: comma convention; strict-versus-infinity pullback justified by the existing isofibration-pullback theorem, Kerodon 033R. Online primary source inspected 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] with $I=N(A)$, $J=N(D)$, functor $N(u)=j_X$, diagram $H=p$ and vertex $T$. Smallness and the quasicategory conditions were checked in step 1, and step 5 verifies its infinity-categorical comma hypothesis at every object of $J$. The conclusion of that cited statement is the restriction map itself, not merely some equivalence between the two spaces. Substituting the definitions of $A,D,u$ gives exactly the map displayed in the item, with constant diagrams restricting to constant diagrams by precomposition. Both functor simplicial sets are quasicategories and their right-pinched mapping spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The criterion requires neither colimit existence in $\mathcal E$ nor a quasicategory structure on $X$, so the asserted scope is unchanged.
